stemLabel: OZ — winger has it on the wall, weak-side D dropped to the net

read.cue: the weak-side defenceman has dropped to the net-front, so the net is covered but the weak-side ice is now open

interaction.prompt: Your winger has the puck on the wall and the weak-side defenceman has dropped to the net. Drag YOURSELF to the open, dangerous ice.

feedback.right: You read the defender. With the weak-side D pulled to the net, the weak-side ice is wide open — get there for the cross-ice look.
feedback.wrong: The net-front is exactly where the defenceman went, so it's covered. The space the D left behind — the weak side — is the open, dangerous ice.

tip: Attack the space the defence leaves. When a defender drops to the net, the ice they vacated is the open one.
why: Reading the off-puck defender is the difference between skating into coverage and finding open ice. The D's choice tells you where to go.
